newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian party HQ deserted as deadline passes.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian party HQ deserted as deadline passes.

text.p: The headquarters of Indonesia's ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri was deserted on Friday as a deadline issued by local authorities to vacate the building passed.
There was no sign that authorities were preparing to take over the headquarters.

An announcement pasted on the gate to the two-storey villa in East Jakarta said the executive board of Megawati's faction of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) had suspended meetings until it had secured permission from the municipality to use the building.
The notice, signed by Megawati aide and member of parliament Tarto Sudiro, said the group's lawyers were in touch with local authorities.
Only four lawyers who represent the PDI faction were in the building, outnumbered by scores of journalists and photographers. They refused to talk to reporters.

Megawati had set up a new office for her faction of the PDI after police raided the official party headquarters on July 27, evicting her supporters and sparking the worst riots in the city of some 10 million people in more than two decades.
She had been ousted from the leadership of the PDI by a government-backed faction in June.

The authorities have warned her against continuing her political activities, and East Jakarta Mayor Sudarsono sent a letter on Monday giving Megawati's faction 72 hours to close the office, saying it violated residential zoning laws.
The municipality delivered another letter on Thursday morning setting a new deadline of 24 hours from receipt of the note.

Sources in the political group said Megawati's lawyers held talks with Sudarsono on Thursday at which it was decided that the municipality would not enforce the vacation notice for one week. The reports could not be independently confirmed.

Political analysts have said the government wanted Megawati, daughter of Indonesia's late founding president Sukarno, out of the PDI leadership for fear she would draw votes away from the ruling Golkar in general elections in May next year.
The Christian-Nationalist PDI, Golkar and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) are the only groups legally entitled to contest the elections.
